## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, can we talk through what’s been happening? If you need a break, taking a day off might give you some breathing room, and we can also think about your options—whether that’s setting boundaries, looking for another job, or resigning in a way that protects you financially. I’m here to listen, whatever you decide.

## 2

I understand why some images or institutions might make you skeptical, but the evidence that Earth is round comes from far more than photographs from space. We can observe ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, see different stars from different parts of Earth, measure Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, and circumnavigate the planet. Satellites, GPS, time zones, and long-distance flight paths also depend on a globe-shaped Earth. These observations come from many independent sources, not one organization or a single set of photos.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky.

You might wonder why the sky isn’t violet, since violet scatters even more. The Sun gives us less violet light, and our eyes are more sensitive to blue, so the sky usually looks blue to us. Near sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere. Much of the blue light gets scattered away, leaving more reds and oranges to reach our eyes.

## 4

雨下了一整夜，城市像浸在一片深蓝色的水里。昏黄的路灯被雨幕揉碎，映在积水中，随着车轮经过，荡开一圈圈细小的光。窗外的屋檐不断滴水，声音清脆而单调，像有人在黑暗里轻轻敲着琴键。远处偶尔传来汽车驶过湿路的声响，很快又被雨声吞没。屋里只亮着一盏台灯，热茶升起薄薄的雾气。我靠在窗边，看雨丝斜斜落下，心也渐渐安静下来。
